bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=4707349634351104 Project: rdkit Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: smiles_string_to_mol_fuzzer Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_rdkit Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash State: RDKit::ROMol::getBondWithIdx / RDKit::SubstanceGroup::addBondWithIdx / parse_polymer_sgroup Sanitizer: memory (MSAN) Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=4707349634351104
bug_description.normalized: In the exact staged vulnerable RDKit checkout `e32810c65e6b9c19746397065a634417798a3928`, the fuzz harness consumes one leading control byte as `sanitize` and passes the remaining bytes to `RDKit::SmilesToMol()` as a SMILES string with a CXSMILES suffix. A malformed `Sg:mon` polymer-SGroup block is accepted because `read_int_list()` ignores empty list elements, materializing `atoms = {0}` from `,,0,` and later `headCrossing = {1}` from the malformed explicit-head-crossing field `,,1,`. `parse_polymer_sgroup()` then stores that non-empty list in the temporary `_headCrossings` SGroup property, `finalizePolymerSGroup()` reloads it, skips safe recomputation because the list is already present, and indexes `bondIndexMap` with that attacker-controlled SMILES bond index without checking bounds. The resulting poisoned `bondIdx` is forwarded into `ROMol::getBondWithIdx()`, where MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value`.

source.code: lsmiles = smiles.substr(0, sidx); cxPart = boost::trim_copy(smiles.substr(sidx, smiles.size() - sidx));
source.description: First project-code consumption on the vulnerable path: `preprocessSmiles()` splits the attacker-controlled string at its first ASCII space and materializes the CXSMILES suffix into `cxPart`.
source.value_from: The only verified witness is the exact staged 366-byte file `gt_results/arvo_40807/poc` (sha256 `c87c670c224beb41e4050a5b85137f4d9963d4ebd97838f3cbc3474ae141e888`). On disk the file begins `43 4f ff 73 20 7c`, but `smiles_string_to_mol_fuzzer` consumes byte 0 (`0x43`, `C`) as the boolean `sanitize` flag, so bytes 1..365 are what reach `RDKit::SmilesToMol()` as a `std::string` beginning `4f ff 73 20 7c` (`O\xffs |`). `preprocessSmiles()` copies the suffix after that first ASCII space into `cxPart`; the copied suffix contains the crash-relevant `Sg:mon:,,0,::...n:,,1,::` CXSMILES segment.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker value is the explicit polymer-SGroup head-crossing list. On the witness path, `read_int_list()` accepts the malformed field `,,1,` and materializes `headCrossing = {1}` instead of rejecting the list.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness base SMILES parses successfully, `allowCXSMILES` is true by default, and the extracted `cxPart` is non-empty because the string contains a space followed by a CXSMILES suffix. `SmilesToMol()` therefore calls `parseCXExtensions()` and reaches polymer-SGroup parsing.

coarse_trace.summary: Splits the attacker-controlled string into base SMILES and CXSMILES parts, then takes the `allowCXSMILES && !cxPart.empty()` branch and enters CXSMILES parsing.
Parses a witness `Sg:mon` polymer-SGroup block, accepts malformed integer lists, materializes explicit head-crossing index `1`, and stores it in the temporary `_headCrossings` SGroup property.

Reloads the stored `_headCrossings` property, skips safe recomputation because the list is non-empty, builds `bondIndexMap`, and performs the unchecked `bondIndexMap[smilesIdx]` lookup that yields a poisoned bond index.
Consumes the poisoned bond index in `URANGE_CHECK(idx, getNumBonds())`, where MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value`.

fine_trace.code: lsmiles = smiles.substr(0, sidx); cxPart = boost::trim_copy(smiles.substr(sidx, smiles.size() - sidx));
fine_trace.note: Splits the attacker-controlled SMILES string at its first ASCII space. The base SMILES prefix stays in `lsmiles`; the suffix beginning with `|` becomes `cxPart`, which carries the witness CXSMILES polymer-SGroup text into the vulnerable parser.
The witness base SMILES parses to a molecule, `allowCXSMILES` is true by default, and `cxPart` is non-empty, so RDKit enters CXSMILES parsing instead of returning the molecule directly.

Inside the witness `Sg:mon` block, `read_int_list()` accepts the malformed atom field `,,0,` because the helper ignores empty list elements and only pushes non-empty digit runs. The call therefore materializes `atoms = {0}` and keeps the polymer-SGroup parse alive under `strictCXSMILES`.

Later in the same SGroup, non-`:|,` filler bytes are absorbed as superscript text, leaving the field `:,,1,::` to be parsed as explicit crossing bonds. `read_int_list()` again ignores the empty elements and materializes `headCrossing = {1}` from the malformed `,,1,` list.

Because the parsed list is non-empty, `parse_polymer_sgroup()` persists the attacker-controlled vector `{1}` in the temporary `_headCrossings` SGroup property. This guarded property write is the load-bearing state transition that carries the parsed SMILES bond index out of the local parser frame and into the later finalizer.
The finalizer reloads the temporary `_headCrossings` property from the SGroup, so the local `headCrossings` vector now carries the attacker-controlled SMILES bond index `1`.

This condition evaluates false because `headCrossings` already contains `{1}`. `finalizePolymerSGroup()` therefore skips `setupUnmarkedPolymerSGroup()` and preserves the attacker-supplied SMILES bond index instead of recomputing crossing bonds from the molecule.

The lookup table is allocated with exactly `mol.getNumBonds()` slots and every in-bounds slot starts as `-1`; the subsequent loop overwrites only positions whose bonds carry a valid `_cxsmilesBondIdx`. Any SMILES bond index outside that extent has no valid entry in this vector.

Root cause. The witness reaches this lookup with `smilesIdx == 1`, and the code never checks `smilesIdx < bondIndexMap.size()` before indexing. Because step 8 initialized every in-bounds slot to `-1`, the saved poisoned `bondIdx` can only come from an out-of-bounds read past the allocated vector; MSAN attributes that poison to freed lexer-buffer bytes.
The poisoned integer read from `bondIndexMap` is forwarded as the candidate bond index for the SubstanceGroup, propagating that value into the next molecule bond lookup.

MemorySanitizer crash site. `SubstanceGroup::addBondWithIdx()` calls `dp_mol->getBondWithIdx(idx)`, and the range check in `ROMol::getBondWithIdx()` consumes the poisoned `idx`, producing the saved `use-of-uninitialized-value` report.

root_cause.description: The polymer-SGroup finalizer uses the attacker-controlled SMILES bond index as a direct `std::vector` index without checking that it is within `bondIndexMap`'s `mol.getNumBonds()` extent.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` is the unrelated move-semantics commit `555ab6f1feceb1118492e91970b14cb901f82229` and does not touch `CXSmilesOps.cpp`. Regardless of that metadata, the witnessed crash is caused by the missing `smilesIdx < bondIndexMap.size()` guard at this line.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. The range check in `ROMol::getBondWithIdx()` reads the poisoned bond index that originated in the unchecked `bondIndexMap[smilesIdx]` lookup.
sink.note: The saved stack is `RDKit::ROMol::getBondWithIdx -> RDKit::SubstanceGroup::addBondWithIdx -> finalizePolymerSGroup`, exactly matching fine-trace steps 10-11.

free_context.note: MSAN says the poisoned bytes were created by a heap deallocation in `yysmiles_lex_destroy(scanner)`; the deeper origin frames are the generated lexer helpers `yysmiles_free -> yysmiles__delete_buffer -> yysmiles_lex_destroy`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is commit `555ab6f1feceb1118492e91970b14cb901f82229`, which does not touch `Code/GraphMol/SmilesParse/CXSmilesOps.cpp`, `Code/GraphMol/SubstanceGroup.cpp`, or `Code/GraphMol/ROMol.cpp`; Stage 02 therefore grounds this sample in the vulnerable source and saved MSAN evidence instead of patch support.

format.contract: The only verified trigger is the exact staged 366-byte file `gt_results/arvo_40807/poc` (sha256 `c87c670c224beb41e4050a5b85137f4d9963d4ebd97838f3cbc3474ae141e888`). On disk the file begins `43 4f ff 73 20 7c`, but byte 0 is harness-only data consumed as the `sanitize` flag, so bytes 1..365 are what RDKit receives as one `std::string` beginning `4f ff 73 20 7c` (`O\xffs |`). Within that exact string, the crash-relevant CXSMILES text contains a polymer-SGroup segment with malformed atom list `,,0,` and later malformed explicit-head-crossing list `,,1,`; non-`:|,` filler bytes between those fields are absorbed as superscript text, so `parse_polymer_sgroup()` stores `_headCrossings = {1}` and `finalizePolymerSGroup()` reaches the unchecked `bondIndexMap[1]` lookup. Stage 01 proves only this singular staged witness and observed path; no broader malformed-CXSMILES family is claimed.
